reason: no_reward - the candidate is not a protocol job but a self-hosted swap/arb executor. A fleet of 9 EOA bots sends it an encoded swap plan (1,380-3,652 bytes of calldata, selectors 0x1608481f / 0x09cef53d); the contract runs WETH/USDC/USDT/WBTC swaps across Uniswap V3 pools and routers, ends flat in tokens, converts its gain to ETH and splits the ETH: ~95% to a fixed address 0x4838b106fce9647bdf1e7877bf73ce8b0bad5f97 and the residual to the caller. The caller's cut is its own arbitrage residual, not a fee paid by a protocol for a public job (it is below the caller's own gas in 2 of 5 sampled non-sweep calls), so a fresh address would have to bring both the plan and the profit; nothing here pays a stranger for calling.
